intro: Phoenix listings advertise 10x10 units from about $48, while typical non-climate 10x10 street rates run about $110–$116/month. Rates are down year over year as new supply opens, but once the move-in special ends and the first existing-customer increase lands, your six-month average still sits well above the banner price. In Phoenix heat, many renters also end up paying the climate-controlled premium.

units.notes: Locker / closet size. Fixed fees dominate the true cost at this size. Climate-controlled ~$48–$49.
Walk-in closet; studio overflow. No reliable lowest-promo figure published for this size (gap). Climate-controlled ~$73.
Most rented size. City average $110, down 3.5% YoY (StorageCafe, Sep 2026); Phoenix metro averages $116, down 6.7% YoY (Storage Stats). Climate-controlled ~$123–$133.
Two-bedroom contents. Estimate: single source (StorageCafe, Sep 2026). Climate-controlled ~$168–$186.
Three-bedroom home or a car. Climate-controlled ~$218–$259.

local_tips: Location drives price: StorageCafe lists Estrella Village (~$102), Alhambra (~$104) and Downtown Phoenix (~$128) among the cheapest areas for a 10x10, while Valley Vista (~$232) and Ahwatukee Foothills (~$189) run highest.
Phoenix rates tend to be lowest around December and highest in September (StorageCafe).
About 497,000 sq ft of new storage is due in Phoenix in 2026 (StorageCafe), and rents are falling — newer facilities often run aggressive move-in specials, so ask what month 5 will cost.
Summer heat makes climate control worth pricing for electronics, wood furniture and documents; it adds roughly 10–25% to the monthly rate.
Extra Space charges a $50 admin fee (per StorageUnitCosts), higher than our $29 default; adjust the calculator if your facility charges more.
